title: I Followed the Festival Water-Refill Policy Into the VIP Cooler

parts.text: I waited at the free refill fountain at 2:44 p.m. in 94-degree heat while a volunteer said it was broken and VIP had water. The posted policy, required by the city, said potable refill within 300 feet of every stage. I was twenty-seven, GA wristband, holding an empty bottle. I photographed the fountain, the policy, and the VIP cooler with staff handing bottles to friends without VIP bands. Then I asked a city health inspector who was already on site for ice cream. At 2:51 the inspector asked the volunteer to define broken.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The inspector wants a definition of broken while friends take VIP bottles.

social.video_title: City-required fountain, VIP cooler for friends — Part 1/2
social.description: 94 degrees, GA band, ice-cream inspector. Broken was a word. Would you have bought a $9 bottle?

parts.text: They uncapped the fountain. It worked. The cooler went back to VIP wristbands. I filled for free, as printed. Friends found the regular line. Broken meant inconvenient. Inspectors like verbs. I watched the next set hydrated. The city sign stayed. $9 bottles still existed for people who like souvenirs. I like tap that is a right. The wristband stayed GA and wet on the inside, correctly.

social.description: Free fill, cooler for actual VIP, verbs. Was broken a guest list?
